properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: hash.js ships in node_modules as elliptic's hashing layer; its SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations are reachable inside elliptic's ECDSA (and by any code that imports it). Not called directly by the application; presence recorded.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: the secp256k1 native library ships with this NFT marketplace's Ethereum toolchain (pulled in by ganache-core/ethereumjs via hardhat+ethers). The marketplace's transactions are ECDSA-secp256k1 signed. Changeable only alongside the EVM protocol itself — the app cannot unilaterally swap the curve its chain uses; the library version is upgradeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: evp_bytestokey ships in the browserify crypto shim (crypto-browserify/browserify-aes) that web3modal/ganache-core pull in for browser builds. Legacy single-round MD5 KDF — present in the shipped node_modules; no direct call site in the application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcrypt-pbkdf (bcrypt-style PBKDF, used by sshpk to parse OpenSSH keys) is a genuinely declared transitive dependency of the ganache-core dev stack in this Hardhat/NFT-marketplace project. The lockfile IS the dependency inventory: the build ships this KDF whether or not the application calls it directly. No first-party call site found — a use question, not a presence question. Changeable here by pruning/upgrading the dev-stack dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: create-ecdh is the browserify crypto shim's ECDH implementation, shipping in the web3modal/browser bundle's crypto-browserify. No direct application call site found — presence is what this entry records; the browser bundle reaches it only through the polyfilled crypto module.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl 0.14.5 provides Ed25519 signatures in the shipped image — genuinely resolved in the lockfile as a transitive dependency (sshpk/bcrypt-pbkdf under ganache-core). Availability inventory: the library ships Ed25519 whether or not this application signs with it. No first-party Ed25519 call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: elliptic's ECDSA implementation on secp256k1 is the signature scheme of the Ethereum JS toolchain (ethereumjs/ganache via hardhat); it ships in node_modules and verifies/signs this marketplace's transactions. The EVM fixes ECDSA-secp256k1 for on-chain recovery — the library here is upgradeable, the chain scheme is not.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: tweetnacl ships in node_modules (0.14.5 under ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3, plus tweetnacl@1.0.3 at top level) and its X25519 scalarmult is available to the Ethereum toolchain. No direct application call site found — presence is what this entry records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry — and actively used: ethers is a direct dependency (package.json) and its keccak256 (original Keccak padding, not SHA3-256) is Ethereum's core hash: every transaction hash, ABI selector and address checksum this app computes runs through it. keccak is protocol-fixed by the EVM; the library version is upgradeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 and @ethersproject/pbkdf2 are genuinely in the resolved tree: ethers v5 uses PBKDF2-SHA512 for BIP39 mnemonic→seed derivation, and the pbkdf2 browser polyfill backs the web3 stack. PBKDF2 is a symmetric KDF (not Shor-vulnerable); its parameters (iteration count) are the interesting part and are set inside ethers, not in first-party code. Availability inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: scrypt-js ships with the build — ethers uses scrypt as the KDF for encrypted JSON keystores (EIP-2335-style password derivation), so any keystore the toolchain opens derives keys through it. Version upgradeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: tweetnacl@0.14.5 (under ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3) provides XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox/one-time auth in the shipped node_modules. No direct application call site; presence is what this entry records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl is the crypto library actually shipped in this build (transitive dep under bcrypt-pbkdf/ganache-core). It implements XSalsa20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption, Ed25519 signatures, X25519 key agreement and SHA-512 — all classical, quantum-vulnerable primitives present in the image. No first-party import of tweetnacl found in application code; presence recorded as availability inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@2.0.4 is a declared lockfile dependency (transitive of the ethereumjs dev stack); it implements the memory-hard scrypt KDF, a symmetric password-based derivation. Quantum-relevant only via Grover's quadratic speedup. Availability inventory; no first-party call site found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 is a declared lockfile dependency (browserify/ethereumjs stack) implementing SHA-1 and SHA-2 family hashes. Availability inventory; no first-party call site found. SHA-1 sites inside this library would merit attention if the library is called with sha1, but that use lives inside dependencies, not this application's code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry — the crypto library itself: elliptic@6.5.4's API surface (ECDSA sign/verify on secp256k1, ECDH, ed25519) ships in node_modules for the Ethereum toolchain. Kept as the library-level entry alongside the algorithm-level ECDSA object ALG-710f61f0, which carries the primitive and migration path. Known CVEs exist for elliptic 6.5.4's signature malleability; version upgradeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.3 is a declared lockfile dependency, transitive of elliptic (which backs the ethers secp256k1 stack); it ships MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160 implementations. Availability inventory — the legacy hashes are present in the shipped image; no first-party call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: the browserify pbkdf2 shim ships in node_modules (dependency of crypto-browserify, used by the web3modal browser bundle and by ethers' keystore KDF). No direct application call site; presence is what this entry records.
